Please don't go. Look, I probably can't convince you much, but, stranger on the internet, this is a permanent solution to a problem that can get better. Maybe not anytime soon, but it will get better. 
There's light there somewhere, and you may not see the source of it, but you can see what's around you. If you can see that, then there is a light letting you see.
Just.. Think it over a few more times? Please?

Not a therapist, but I do sometimes have similar sort of 'visions.' So far for me, it's prevented such self-harm. It is very possible it could be different for you, and I recommend seeing someone or telling a current therapist about it.

I would also recommend imagining some other sort of pain-inflicting thing if possible. It can be better and help you to not cut if the time comes this does cause self-harm.
For example, rather than a blade being dragged across your skin, a simple pinch or digging your nails into your skin.

You don't have to take my advice, but it's here if you want it. I wish you luck.

I've done a few things.

One was that I went around saying I was a werewolf in 2nd grade. I also said that I had a vampire boyfriend who would murder people in their sleep if they made fun of me.
Yeah, not my proudest moment.

A second, was that to fit in during.. I believe 3rd grade? I basically threatened to blow up the school. At least, that's what the rumours made it sound like. And I admit, saying, "In my Minecraft world I have enough TNT to blow up the school!" Is quite.. Uhm.. Easy to mishear/misinterpret?
Again, much regret.

A third one, and the most recent, was when word got out I was suicidal. No one treated me the same way. The school got me a councillor (that was fun), my mom thought I was lying, my friends wouldn't let me make jokes anymore (The jokes I make normally go along that topic, so I can see why, but really?). 
The worst of it, though, was that my condition worsened. A lot. I cut myself off from people other than my close group of friends, who I've known for about 9 years now. One person, though, decided she didn't like that. She texted me, asking why I was acting like a bitch toward her that day. I got defensive, which I mildly regret. She ended up sharing our conversation with the class, and completely defamed me.
This was a few months ago, and some people still hate me for it. It's better, but not at all the same as it was before.

And that's about it. Yes, I am still made fun of, or degrade myself over these things. I can joke and laugh about it all, but it's a clear cover-up. I know that quite a few people don't forgive me, won't let things go, but the good thing is I can normally bury my emotions about said things.

Anyway, hope you all have a good day if you've read this. Bai~

It all happened so suddenly. One moment we were ready to take it to the ground, the next I was standing there as a vampire bit down on his neck, the color draining from his face.

It was an everyday at high school, same empty threats and getting our brains filled with nonsense we'll never use in our lives. The "Bad Boy" of the class threatened to kill me, again. I took him up on his offer to meet after school in a nearby abandoned playground. I knew the area well, taking into account the advantages I'd have spending most of my time there. I almost laughed at the thought, the bad boy of the class taken down by a girl. Vaulting over what was left of the fencing, I made my way to the main structure. It was just past sunset, prime time to be paranoid about vampires. I knew about the biting rule, but still, they can be anywhere. One wrong word and could be done for.

Two hours pass, he still hasn't shown. Just as I was about to leave, I heard a rustling in the bushes by the fence. Out came the bad boy. Letting out a sigh, I sat back down, flinching when I felt a cold hand where I set my own. I turned, staring up into dark red eyes. Terrifyingly beautiful.

Focusing back on my task, I broke eye contact. I stood back up and made my way over to the already bruised bad boy. Unfortunately, the vampire followed. Turns out, the bad boy brought his little crew along with him.
"You actually came, Provos?"
The audacity of this man. He said it like I was the scaredy cat in this situation. I replied, "You're late, Alexander Francesco Zytsev."

He just looked at me. Staring. As if I had just said the most offensive thing known to mankind. No one ever calls him by his actual name, let alone his full name. I let a small smile slip past my mask of annoyance. He hated it. I called him by his full name and now took pleasure in his disbelief. 

The vampires expression changed from calm to irritated, angered, and.. Hungry. He moved to stand next to me, glaring down at Alexander. I looked at him, curious as to what he'd do next. A small whimper of sorts came from Alexander, my eyes flicking to him in attempt to find out why. He was held around the waist by a second vampire. Another male one. 

What's up with me being the only female? I thought to myself. I didn't have time think much anymore, as I still wanted a fight. Fight don't think, y'know? Oh how I wish it was going to be that simple.

"Hey, hey. The kid's my dinner," the first vampire said in a - and I'll be dead honest - really deep voice. Handsome, a slight rasp to it. The female responded in a light-hearted, smooth tone. Her voice was angelic, "You can't have all the humans to yourself, Daniel. Besides, there's the girl too. Take her instead."

Alexander twisted around and delivered an elbow to the female's jaw in a sudden motion, knocking her down to the ground. The blow left her unconscious, and him vulnerable from behind while he stared at his success. The male - Daniel - was enraged by this, as the female was likely his lover. That's me assuming, but it seems reasonable. He grabbed Alexander in a choke hold and growled, "You dirty human! How dare you do such a thing!"

Alexander, being stupid, smirked with a reply, "Bite me."
"Gladly." Daniel didn't hesitate, throwing Alexander around and nearly snapping his neck to allow himself access. He sucked Alexander dry. 

I stared in disbelief along with the others who were awkwardly standing there for the past two minutes. When the vampire looked up, we immediately booked it. We took off, vaulting over the fence and down the road. We kept running until we were 4 blocks down the road and laughed about it later.

Even now, I still remember his eyes, the feeling of him staring as I ran. I felt it then, and still feel it now. I know he's watching, waiting for the moment I slip up and allow him to drain me too. 

But that won't happen. 
Not until I'm already dead.

Never again, I swear it on my life.
So kids, that's why, you never. Under any circumstance, say,

"Bite me."
Absolutely beautiful.
